destinations.name: Bandarban
destinations.description: Bandarban is a hill district famous for its misty peaks, tribal culture, and lush valleys, offering some of the most scenic trekking routes in Bangladesh.
destinations.weather_notes: Cool and dry in winter; heavy monsoon rain June-September
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Hill resorts and cottages in Nilgiri/Milanchari area
destinations.travel_tips: Carry warm clothing for early morning hill viewpoints; roads can be steep and winding
destinations.permits_required: Special permit required for Thanchi, Ruma and deep hill-tract routes

destinations.name: Cox's Bazar
destinations.description: Cox's Bazar offers an unbroken 120km sandy beach along with island getaways like Saint Martin and Inani.
destinations.weather_notes: Warm and dry in winter; rough seas and monsoon rains June-September
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Beachfront hotels along Marine Drive and Kolatoli
destinations.travel_tips: Sunrise at Sugandha Point and sunset at Laboni Point are must-sees
destinations.permits_required: None for the mainland beach; NOC required for Saint Martin during restricted seasons

destinations.name: Rangamati
destinations.description: Rangamati sits on the shores of Kaptai Lake, offering boat rides, hanging bridges, and indigenous Chakma culture.
destinations.weather_notes: Warm days, cool evenings in winter; heavy rainfall in monsoon
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Lake-view resorts and floating cottages near the hanging bridge
destinations.travel_tips: Book a boat early for a full-day Kaptai Lake and Shuvolong tour
destinations.permits_required: ID verification required for some restricted zones

content.hero_title: Built by people who call Bangladesh home
content.hero_subtitle: Atithi (অতিথি) started with a simple frustration: booking a domestic trip meant middlemen, vague pricing, and cash changing hands with no record. We built the agency we wished existed — local hosts, honest pricing, and a payment system that leaves nothing to dispute.
story_paragraphs: Most domestic travel in Bangladesh is organized through word-of-mouth recommendations, social media groups, or informal fixers. Prices shift depending on who's asking, booking confirmations are a verbal promise, and if something goes wrong, there's no recourse.
We wanted something different: trips you could book with complete confidence, hosted by people from the actual communities you're visiting, with clear itineraries and receipts for every taka paid.
Every route we offer is one we've traveled ourselves multiple times — staying at the same eco-cottages, riding the same wooden engine boats, and breaking bread with the same village hosts.
content.mission_text: To connect travelers with authentic, dignified local hosting across every district of Bangladesh — backed by transparent pricing, flexible payments, and human support.

values.title: Radical transparency
values.description: Every taka is accounted for — the price you see is the price you pay, and every payment is confirmed on both sides.

values.title: Local, always
values.description: No outsourced guides, no foreign templates. Every host is Bangladeshi, and every itinerary is built around real local knowledge.

values.title: Hospitality first
values.description: Atithi — "guest" — is central to Bengali culture. We host you the way we'd host family, not process you like a booking number.

values.title: Considered detail
values.description: From the ridge walk only locals know to the candlelit dinner arranged without being asked — the small things are the trip.

content.payment_title: How your money is handled, end to end
content.payment_description: Pay in full or pay a small advance through bKash, Nagad, Rocket, or card at booking. If you paid partially, the remaining balance is settled on the day of the tour — either your host scans your personal QR code, or you log in and pay it yourself. The moment it clears, both you and our team get a WhatsApp and email confirmation, so there's a clean record of what was paid, when, on both sides.
